name: Iterations
one_liner: A fixed timebox producing a stable, potentially shippable slice of solution.
purpose: An Agile iteration is a period of time within a project in which the A-PCT produces a stable, potentially shippable part of the solution together with any supporting documentation or deliverables. Iterations are timeboxed: the duration is fixed and the scope of the content is actively managed to meet that schedule. Each iteration produces a product increment that brings the system one step closer to the final product.
meta: Predefined, timeboxed and recurring period in which the working solution is created (glossary, p. 104)
One to four weeks; in PM²-Agile every iteration has the same duration
Duration is fixed; scope of the content is actively managed
Iteration Planning (first activity) · Daily Stand-up · Release Planning (≥ once) · Review + Retrospective (last day)
A product increment plus a refined, prioritised Work Items List
The Iteration Plan artefact (§7.2.2.3, p. 80) — not a ceremony row

items: A period in which the A-PCT produces a stable, potentially shippable part of the solution
Plus any other necessary supporting documentation or deliverables
Timeboxed: duration fixed, content actively managed to meet the schedule
Produces a product increment — the system is 'grown', not assembled part after part
Properly planned: goals well-defined, acceptance criteria established, tasks and responsibilities clear, progress transparent through agreed metrics

diagram.sec: 2. Why every iteration is the same length (p. 35)
items: Establishes the 'heartbeat' of the project
Reduces overall uncertainty — we cannot predict everything, but we control when an iteration ends
Helps understand the project team's performance
Small and regular iterations also allow decisions to be postponed to the last responsible moment (Set Based Design)
Implement the highest-priority Work Items from the Work Items List
Address the most critical risks, so each iteration adds value while reducing uncertainty
Dedicate a portion of its time to lay the foundation for the next iteration — this is where Design Blocks play their role
Integrate continuously: unit-tested components integrated into regular builds, submitted for integration testing

diagram.sec: 4. The three ways of exposing work (p. 20)
items: Exposure of Work Items — when the team completes one or more items; keep it light, notify the PrOw, request feedback
Exposure at the end of an Iteration — supports the Iteration Review; includes all items deemed ready for review
Release — an agreed Solution Increment delivered to client and users, containing all Done Work Items from several prior iterations
The sum of all Work Items exposed is what makes a great Iteration Review
Coordinate: Iteration Planning is the first activity; Daily Stand-up each day; Release Planning at least once
Implement: build, integrate, expose Work Items to the PrOw as they become ready
Review: Iteration Review then Iteration Retrospective on the last day
Close: Iteration Plan updated with the outcome; refined and prioritised WIL handed to the next Iteration Planning

diagram.sec: 6. What comes out of an iteration
items: A validated increment demonstrated against the iteration goal
Accepted / rejected verdicts per Work Item against acceptance criteria and the Definition of Done
New velocity data, which is reflected in the Release Plan
Retrospective actions, placed in the Work Items List like any other item

fields.what: A period in which the A-PCT produces a stable, potentially shippable part of the solution, with supporting documentation and deliverables.
fields.pollux: Iteration 7 runs Mon 02 Apr to Fri 13 Apr 2029, ten calendar working days.

fields.what: The practice of constraining the time for an activity. The iteration duration is fixed; the scope of its content is what flexes.
fields.pollux: Two weeks, fixed for all 26 POLLUX iterations — never extended to fit scope.

fields.what: Every PM²-Agile iteration has the same length, for three reasons: project heartbeat, reduced uncertainty, and understanding team performance.
fields.pollux: Two weeks even across Easter; the holiday cuts capacity, not the timebox.

fields.what: The output of one iteration: prototypes or specific parts of the system developed or updated, bringing the system one step closer to the final product.
fields.pollux: Iteration 7 adds exposure by instrument to the read-only member-state view.

fields.what: Stable and demonstrable at the end of the iteration; not necessarily deployed. Deployment to users is what makes a Release.
fields.pollux: Instrument view is potentially shippable in April; it ships with Release 2 in June.

fields.what: The well-defined goal of the iteration, proposed by the PrOw from the prioritised WIL, committed to by the A-PCT, and evaluated at the Review.
fields.pollux: "A Risk analyst can break exposure down by instrument, traceable to the lending platform."

fields.what: The subset of the WIL planned for the iteration, plus start and end dates, the Iteration Goal, sync points with other teams, and related risks and issues.
fields.who: TeCo R · PM A · PrOw C
fields.pollux: One Iteration Plan per iteration; opened at planning, closed at the review.

fields.what: Every iteration starts with the Iteration Planning ceremony and ends with the Iteration Review; that arc is captured in a single Iteration Plan.
fields.pollux: Iteration Plan 7 records the Easter Monday holiday and the 189-hour capacity.

fields.what: Criteria by which a work item is evaluated against client expectations. Commonly all-or-nothing: all pass and the item is a candidate for Done, or it is not Done.
fields.who: PrOw defines · ATeM builds to them
fields.pollux: Curie's criteria are the reason nobody argues at the review.

fields.what: The team's standard for finished work, checked at the Iteration Review. Meeting acceptance criteria alone does not make an item Done.
fields.pollux: POLLUX adds accessibility and a data-protection check to the DoD.

fields.what: Workshops within Release Planning where ATeMs sketch low-fidelity prototypes until common understanding is reached; high-fidelity ones then go to stakeholders.
fields.who: ATeMs facilitate · PrOw presents · BM/BIG validate
fields.pollux: Where Risk, the Board and Finance stop describing three different reports.

fields.what: Each iteration must dedicate a portion of its time to laying the foundation for the work of the following iteration.
fields.pollux: Iteration 7 refines the reconciliation-panel stories that Iteration 8 will build.

fields.what: Light-touch delivery of a completed item into a standard test environment; the ATeM notifies the PrOw and requests feedback. Formalism kept to a minimum.
fields.pollux: Curie sees each instrument-view story the day it is ready, not on the 13th.

fields.what: Unit-tested components are integrated to generate a build submitted for integration testing; regular builds spread integration problems across the cycle.
fields.pollux: Broken-build percentage is one of the metrics collected at the retrospective.

fields.what: The number of story points associated with stories finished over a timeboxed iteration; used to test Release Plan feasibility.
fields.who: ATeMs generate · TeCo reflects it in the Release Plan
fields.pollux: Average 34 points over iterations 4–6; only 21 accepted in iteration 7.

fields.what: The prioritised list of everything to be built — user stories, enabler stories, defects. The main driver of the project and the source of every iteration's content.
fields.pollux: Curie owns it; Hopper supports; Einstein feeds enablers into it.

fields.what: A technical work item that supports the implementation of the business solution; identified by the A-PCT, typically explained to the PrOw by the ArOw.
fields.pollux: WIL-121, the nightly instrument reference sync from the lending platform.

fields.what: The hours each ATeM can dedicate to the iteration, after holidays, public holidays and other events, usually with an allowance for unplanned work.
fields.pollux: Nine working days × 7 hours = 63 hours, less 10% for unplanned events.

fields.what: An iteration whose activities prepare a release rather than add features. Planned and run like any regular iteration, with the proper ceremonies.
fields.pollux: Iteration 6 shipped Release 1 on 29 Mar 2029 as a Transition Iteration.

traps: The timebox is fixed and scope flexes — never the other way round.
"Potentially shippable" is not "released"; a release needs delivery to users.
Exposing Work Items during the iteration does not replace the Iteration Review.
All iterations are the same length, including Transition Iterations.
Retrospective actions are iteration content: they go into the Work Items List.
